note: Independent source rejudgment against full RFC 9552 Section 5.2.3.1: the OSPF Route Type TLV MUST accompany an advertisement when the underlying LSA signals the type explicitly or another LSA for the same prefix determines it. The source further specifies resolving Extended Prefix external/NSSA classes and type zero from base LSAs. Read both tagged tests and producer chain. The live LSDB publisher test installs actual Router, Summary Network, AS External and NSSA LSAs plus an opaque-marked Extended Prefix; ten cases demand exactly one correlated advertisement for router 2.2.2.2 with exact type 1..6, including cross-area NSSA. Its opaque guard excludes a base-only result. publishBGPLSLocked processes bases before extensions; extendedV2Prefix consumes v2PrefixRouteTypes, which correlates prefix/router identity and external metric type. The exporter test independently reconciles a native OSPF snapshot and asserts TLV 264 value 1 in captured NLRI. These compose source-publisher and encoder boundaries; this is not a live BGP-peer test and the wire test does not exhaust all six values. The single-positive annotation is sound for mandatory origination, not an exemption when the underlying value is zero. The exhaustive-ignore directive only documents the fixture's restricted LSA types. Verdict enforced. No execution or replay freshness claimed.
